title: Temple of Hibis
visualBrief: Standing Hibis temple exterior: lower roofed stone rear body with cavetto cornice, actual front/side doorways and shallow square wall sockets; higher roofless portico with varied palm/bell/bud capitals, heavy perimeter beams, low screen walls and central open doorframe. Occupied platform/short approaches and one pictured freestanding carved entrance gateway. Original simplified bands/petals/winged-disc vocabulary over shared sandstone, no copied inscriptions/relief atlas. Internal support/room inventory, other distant gates/quay, palms, precinct walls and temporary scaffold are not claimed authored.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Exact-QID OSMway98894290/Q4115642 is a226.9x157.5m archaeological precinct boundary, not a temple roof. Standard PMTiles has no building polygons here. Named ruinsPOI35184470983133 fixes approximate primary body center[-38.851238986624736,-3.2655914214297206] relative to anchor30.555698636,25.476418144. Named attractionPOI35184470983122 and original eastern reference point align an approximately northeast approach; internal main bearing-0.5118553083174939rad follows that line, rather than the precinct boundary axis. Ordinary east/south photos support signed front facing. Main envelope/column/screen allocation remains picture-led, about10m/20degree uncertainty. The single pictured gateway is allocated at the original eastern reference point[34.47281716039595,-43.126395247428185] on that approach with about25m location uncertainty; exact gate association is not mapped. No native building shell is replaced.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Picture/map approximation: primary rear body26x17m (localX-18..8), roof/cavetto to6.9m above local floor. Open portico13x17m (X8..21), exterior support/beam grid with four stations per exposed edge, columns to7.1m/architrave-cavetto to8.55m, low2.8m screens and6m open central frame. Rear small square sockets at about2.7m and real south doorway; no full portico roof. Freestanding gateway approximately5.2m wide/2.8m deep and6.3m high with2.2x4.5m passage. Exact dimensions/capital/support inventory, relief, roof details and heights remain picture-led visualization estimates, not an archaeological survey.
